hero.eyebrow: v{{version}} — Git actions + full GitLab & Bitbucket support
hero.sub: Recrest is a native desktop app that brings your <1>local Git repositories</1>, their working‑tree status, merge requests and CI checks from <3>GitHub</3>, <5>GitLab</5> and <7>Bitbucket</7> into a single, calm place.

demo.title: Recrest live demo
demo.hint: Seeded sample data — no backend, nothing leaves your browser.

privacy.title: Nothing leaves your machine.
privacy.body: Recrest reads your Git repositories directly from disk and talks to GitHub, GitLab & Bitbucket APIs from your machine — nothing in between.

noServers.title: No Recrest servers.
noServers.body: No telemetry, no analytics. Your repo list never leaves your disk.

keychain.title: Tokens stay in your OS keychain.
keychain.body: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service — never ours.

native.title: Native & tiny.
native.body: ~12 MB bundle, <80 MB RAM idle. Rust core, web‑tech UI.

offline.title: Works offline.
offline.body: Local status keeps updating. Remote state resumes when you're back online.

contribute.title: Built in the open. <1>Help shape</1> it.
contribute.body: Recrest is MIT‑licensed and developed on GitHub. Whether you fix a typo or rewrite the diff engine — you're welcome here.

issue.title: File an issue
issue.body: Bug reports, feature requests and "that felt off" observations — all welcome.

pr.title: Open a pull request
pr.body: Rust, TypeScript or design tokens — the codebase is friendly and reviewed fast.

discussion.title: Join the discussion
discussion.body: GitHub Discussions is where we talk through upcoming designs and trade‑offs.

footer.tagline: A quiet desktop dashboard for developers who work across many Git repositories. Made with care, shared under MIT.

download.title: Download Recrest
download.subtitle: Native desktop builds for macOS, Windows and Linux.

disclaimer.title: Unsigned builds — and why
disclaimer.body: Recrest is a free, open-source project, so we don't pay for Apple's Developer Program or a Windows EV code-signing certificate — the installers are not signed. On first launch your operating system (macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen) will warn you as a result. The download is safe as long as you get it straight from our GitHub Releases using the buttons below. Each installer has its own first-run steps — follow the notes under your platform.

download.copyCommand: Copy the install command to the clipboard

osSub.macos: macOS 11 Big Sur or later · Apple Silicon and Intel

install.heading: First-run instructions
macos: Open Finder and go to Downloads.
Double-click the .dmg file to mount it.
Drag Recrest to your Applications folder.
On first launch macOS may block the app because it is unsigned. Right-click (or Ctrl-click) the app in Applications and choose Open, then click Open in the dialog.
Alternatively, remove the quarantine flag in Terminal: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Recrest.app`
windows: If Windows SmartScreen appears, click More info and then Run anyway.
Follow the setup wizard and launch Recrest from the Start menu.
linux: Fedora / RHEL (.rpm): `sudo rpm -i recrest-v*.rpm` (or `sudo dnf install ./recrest-v*.rpm`)
Flathub: `flatpak install flathub com.soft_ventures.Recrest` — once the package is approved there. Updates itself automatically afterwards.
Arch (AUR): `paru -S recrest-bin` installs the prebuilt package. `recrest` builds from source instead, `recrest-git` from the current development branch.
Updates: .deb and .rpm have to be re-downloaded by hand — there is no APT or DNF repository. Through the AUR packages, pacman updates Recrest like any other package.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.subtitle: Information pursuant to Art. 13 GDPR.
privacy.intro: This privacy policy explains how the Recrest project handles personal data when you visit this website. Using this website is generally possible without providing any personal data. The Recrest desktop application transmits no personal data to us by default; optional crash reports can be enabled in the application's settings (see the "Crash reports from the desktop application" section).

sections.crashReporting: Crash reports from the desktop application

privacy.hostingBody: This website is hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P Kelly Jr St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). GitHub may process request metadata such as your IP address, the user agent of your browser and the time of the request for the purpose of operating the service and protecting it from abuse. The processing takes place on the basis of Art. 6 (1) lit. f GDPR (legitimate interest in providing a secure and stable service). For further information see the <1>GitHub Privacy Statement</1>.
privacy.fontsBody: The fonts used on this website (Inter and JetBrains Mono) are served directly from our own origin. No external font services such as Google Fonts are embedded, so loading the fonts transmits no IP address or other personal data to third parties.
privacy.storageBody: This website stores your display preferences in your browser's local storage so they persist on your next visit — specifically your language preference (key "recrest-landing-locale") and your colour theme (key "recrest-landing-theme"). This storage is technically necessary for the bilingual operation and theme selection of the site and does not require consent under § 25 (2) TDDDG. The data stays on your device only, is never transmitted to us and is not used for tracking. We do not use cookies.
privacy.logsBody: We do not run our own analytics, trackers or comparable services. No personal data is collected by us through this website for analytics or marketing purposes.
privacy.crashReportingBody: The separately installable Recrest desktop application can send optional crash reports via the Sentry service (Functional Software, Inc.). This feature is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled in the application's settings (opt-in). Only after you enable it are technical diagnostic data such as the error message, stack trace and operating-system and version details transmitted in the event of an error, in order to fix bugs (Art. 6 (1) lit. a GDPR). No crash reporting takes place on this website.
privacy.externalBody: This site links to external services such as GitHub repositories, GitHub Discussions and release downloads. When you follow a link, the linked service receives your request and may process your data according to its own privacy policy.
privacy.rightsBody: Under the GDPR you have the right to access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17) and restriction of processing (Art. 18), to object (Art. 21) and to data portability (Art. 20). Please contact the data controller listed in the imprint to exercise these rights. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your personal data infringes the GDPR (Art. 77 GDPR).
privacy.changesBody: We may update this privacy policy when the technical or legal situation changes. The current version is always available on this page.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.subtitle: Our commitment to digital accessibility — aligned with WCAG 2.1 AA.
accessibility.statusBody: Recrest aims to meet the <1>Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA</1>. Both the website and the desktop application are tested continuously against this standard through self-assessment, using automated (Axe) and manual checks. At the time of writing, no critical, serious or moderate violations are known.
accessibility.featuresIntro: The Recrest desktop application ships with a range of features that make it usable for as many people as possible:

featureList.dyslexia: A typeface optimised for readers with dyslexia (OpenDyslexic) can be enabled in the settings.
featureList.contrast: A high-contrast mode improves the legibility of text and controls.
featureList.motion: Motion and animations can be reduced; the system setting "prefers-reduced-motion" is respected automatically.
featureList.underline: Links can be permanently underlined for better recognisability.
featureList.scale: Text and interface size can be scaled freely to suit your needs.

accessibility.scopeBody: This statement applies to the Recrest landing page and the Recrest desktop application in its current version.
accessibility.knownBody: We are not aware of any content that fails WCAG 2.1 AA at this time. Should you nevertheless encounter barriers, we would be glad to hear about it (see "Feedback").
accessibility.legalBody: Recrest is a free, open-source project and as such is not subject to any statutory accessibility obligation under the German Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). We provide this statement voluntarily because accessible software matters to us.
accessibility.feedbackBody: If you encounter barriers on this website or in the desktop application, please contact us at <1>{{email}}</1>. We will respond as quickly as possible.
accessibility.created: This accessibility statement was created and last reviewed on {{date}}.
